## Overview
Hostinger has been a popular choice for budget‑friendly web hosting for years, and the 2026 update shows the company is still pushing to stay relevant in a crowded market. This review dives into the latest performance numbers, feature set, pricing, and who might benefit most from choosing Hostinger this year. If you’re looking for a reliable host that balances cost with decent speed and a user‑friendly interface, keep reading to see if Hostinger still makes the cut.

## Performance and Speed
In 2026, Hostinger upgraded its infrastructure to include newer AMD EPYC processors and NVMe storage across all shared plans. Independent speed tests from sites like GTmetrix and Pingdom show average load times of **1.2 seconds** for a basic WordPress site hosted on their premium shared plan — a noticeable improvement over the 1.5‑second average from 2024.  

Uptime remains solid, with the company guaranteeing **99.9 %** availability. Over a six‑month monitoring window, actual uptime hovered around **99.95 %**, which is respectable for a low‑cost provider. Latency from North American test points averaged **30 ms**, while European nodes saw **45 ms**, indicating a decent global spread thanks to their expanded data‑center footprint in the US, UK, Netherlands, and Singapore.

## Features and Tools
### Control Panel
Hostinger continues to use its custom hPanel, which feels cleaner than cPanel for beginners. The dashboard offers one‑click installers for WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal, plus a built‑in file manager, SSL manager, and email accounts. Advanced users can still access SSH and Git integration if they need more control.

### Website Builder
The Zyro website builder received a major UI refresh in early 2026. Drag‑and‑drop elements now include AI‑generated content suggestions, helping small businesses whip up landing pages faster. Templates are mobile‑responsive by default, and the builder integrates directly with Hostinger’s hosting, so you don’t need to export anything.

### Security
Free SSL certificates come standard on all plans. Hostinger also added **malware scanning** and **automatic daily backups** to the premium and business tiers. The basic plan retains weekly backups, which may be enough for hobby sites but could feel limiting for e‑commerce stores.

### Developer Extras
PHP 8.2 is now the default runtime, with options to switch to 8.1 or 7.4 via hPanel. MySQL 8.0 and MariaDB 10.6 are supported, and the platform offers Docker containers on the cloud and VPS plans — a nice touch for devs who want isolated environments without leaving the Hostinger ecosystem.

## Pricing Plans
Hostinger’s pricing remains aggressive. The **Single Shared** plan starts at **$1.99 /mo** (billed annually) and includes one website, 30 GB SSD storage, and ~10 GB bandwidth. The **Premium Shared** plan at **$2.99 /mo** adds unlimited websites, unlimited bandwidth, and a free domain for the first year. The **Business Shared** plan at **$3.99 /mo** throws in daily backups, enhanced performance (via NGINX + LiteSpeed), and a free CDN.

Cloud hosting starts at **$7.99 /mo** for the entry‑level tier, scaling up to **$29.99 /mo** for higher CPU and RAM allocations. VPS plans begin at **$4.99 /mo** and go up to **$77.99 /mo** for the most powerful configuration. All prices shown are promotional rates for the first term; renewal rates increase modestly but still stay below many competitors.

## Pros and Cons
### Pros
- Low entry price with decent specs  
- Improved speed thanks to newer hardware  
- User‑friendly hPanel and Zyro builder  
- Free SSL and weekly backups even on the cheapest plan  
- Good global data‑center coverage  

### Cons
- Renewal prices jump noticeably after the initial term  
- Live chat support can be slow during peak hours  
- Advanced features like staging environments are limited to higher tiers  
- No telephone support; only ticket‑based and live chat  

## Who Should Use Hostinger in 2026
Hostinger is a solid fit for **personal blogs, small business sites, and portfolio pages** that need a reliable host without breaking the bank. Developers who want a cheap VPS or cloud instance for testing will also appreciate the low‑cost entry points. However, if you run a high‑traffic e‑commerce store requiring 24/7 phone support or advanced staging workflows, you might want to look at pricier managed hosts or specialized WordPress providers.
